xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4949: Agent MCP and bots (W-CONN1): Machine: connector credential, pairing intents, exchange

plan.title: Agent MCP and bots (W-CONN1): Machine: connector credential, pairing intents, exchange
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: This is one leaf child issue (W-CONN1) of epic PAN-4927, already sized by the epic. Its 26 files include 5 test files, the no-loss matrix data file and 2 docs; the production change is the connector credential kind plus the only routes that mint, list and revoke it. Splitting the credential from the exchange would ship a credential kind nothing can create, and epic AC-20 can only be verified with both halves, so the work stays in one issue with eight small items.

narratives.Problem: A self-hosted bot needs a credential to reach one Overdeck machine through the end-to-end encrypted channel. Today the registry knows only device, token, machine and phone records; a phone record always carries the full phone scopes, and a token record authenticates on plain sockets, so a stolen token would work without the bot's key. There is also no way to issue a pairing code that only a connector can redeem: the same odp_ code pairs a browser as an admin device, a machine or a phone.
narratives.Proposal: Add a 'connector' access-token kind bound to the connector's link key (connectorKey) and client id, minted only with operator-chosen scopes from CONNECTOR_SCOPE_CHOICES and resolved only inside a link-mode channel from that key (scopes filtered again at resolve time). Store a pairing intent { name, scopes, expiresAt } by pairingId when the operator issues a connector pairing code (root only), return an overdeck-connector:/pair# string built in @overdeck/contracts, and redeem it once through POST /api/connectors/exchange over a pairing channel. Add root-only list and revoke routes plus a connector self-revoke, make the handshake pin and revocation closers know connectors, refuse connector codes in the browser, machine and phone exchanges, advertise capabilities.connector, and document it all in docs/DASHBOARD-AUTH.md and docs/ANYWHERE-ARCHITECTURE.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- The connector process, pan mcp connector, its home files and its local endpoint (W-CONN2).
- Any frontend change: the Connect a bot dialog and bot list (W-BOT1).
- Directory changes for platform node (W-DIR1, PAN-4948).
- Mintlify pages (configuration/bots.mdx, cli/mcp.mdx, anywhere.mdx) and docs/CONNECT-SERVICE.md (W-DOC).
- Pruning revoked connector records.
- Persisting pairing intents across a dashboard restart.
- Any change to the link fence, fleet routes or the linked-conversation proxy.
- Any change to how token, device, machine or phone credentials resolve, apart from the connector-code refusal in their exchanges.
- Raising any file-size allowlist row.

autoDecisions.summary: The connector pairing string builder and parser live in packages/contracts/src/connector-pairing.ts, not only in the server module.
autoDecisions.rationale: W-CONN2 lives in src/lib/mcp/connector and cannot import from src/dashboard/server; the phone link already sets this pattern in packages/contracts/src/phone-pairing.ts.

autoDecisions.summary: The resolved connector credential carries connectorKey, like the phone credential carries phoneKey.
autoDecisions.rationale: The self-revoke handler needs the key to close the channel; it adds no exposure because the key is the channel's own proved key.

autoDecisions.summary: The resolver filters a connector record's scopes to CONNECTOR_SCOPE_CHOICES.
autoDecisions.rationale: Defense in depth on a security boundary: a hand-edited record with admin still grants nothing outside the allowed set, which makes epic AC-20 'carries only its chosen scopes' hold even for a tampered file.

autoDecisions.summary: POST /api/pairing/exchange checks for a connector code before consuming the code and counts the refusal as a pairing failure; the machine and phone exchanges check channel.pairingId after the handshake already consumed the code.
autoDecisions.rationale: A mistaken browser paste should not burn the connector's code; the pairing-channel paths cannot avoid the burn because the handshake consumes it first.

autoDecisions.summary: The pairing route always adds read:state to the chosen scopes.
autoDecisions.rationale: DELETE /api/connectors/self needs read:state; without the floor a connector could not log out.

autoDecisions.summary: The intent is taken (removed) at the start of the exchange, before the body is parsed.
autoDecisions.rationale: The handshake already consumed the code, so the intent can never be used again either way; taking it first gives one simple single-use rule.

autoDecisions.summary: POST /api/connectors/pairing, GET /api/connectors and DELETE /api/connectors/:id accept only the internal token or the root session, checked in the handler.
autoDecisions.rationale: An unlisted route needs admin, which an admin-scoped token or device also holds; the epic says root only, and pairing.ts and access-tokens.ts already check root this way.
The epic already decomposed the work; this leaf issue cannot ship its credential kind without the routes that mint it, and 8 of the 26 files are tests, test data and docs.

narrative.Action: Follow PRD .pan/drafts/PAN-4949.md work item W-1 exactly. In src/lib/access-token-records.ts: add 'connector' to AccessTokenKind (line 19); add the optional connectorKey field; reword the clientId comment to 'phone and connector only'; in isRecord accept kind 'connector', require connectorKey (64 lowercase hex, MACHINE_KEY_HEX) and clientId (UUID_V4) and no machineKey/environmentId/access/phoneKey/pushKey/agent fields on it, and refuse connectorKey on every other kind. In src/lib/access-tokens.ts: export CONNECTOR_SCOPE_CHOICES = ['read:state','read:conversations','tell','operate','approve'] and BOT_DEFAULT_SCOPES = ['read:state','read:conversations','tell'] next to PHONE_TOKEN_SCOPES (line 100); add connectorKey to CreateAccessTokenInput; add the connector branch to createAccessToken (messages in the PRD) and refuse connectorKey on every other kind; extend findActiveChannelTokenByKey (lines 422-427) to match kind 'connector' by connectorKey and update its comment and the file header. access-tokens.ts grows by at most 45 lines. Write tests/unit/lib/access-tokens-connector.test.ts with the cases listed in W-1.

narrative.Action: Follow PRD W-3 and D-3. Create packages/contracts/src/connector-pairing.ts in the contracts style of phone-pairing.ts (no semicolons, double quotes), importing PHONE_PAIR_ENVIRONMENT_ID_RE, PHONE_PAIR_MACHINE_KEY_RE and PHONE_PAIR_CODE_RE from ./phone-pairing. Export CONNECTOR_PAIR_SCHEME = "overdeck-connector", CONNECTOR_PAIR_LINK_VERSION = 1, CONNECTOR_PAIR_LINK_PREFIX = "overdeck-connector:/pair#", interface ConnectorPairLinkInput { environmentId; machineKeyHex; code }, buildConnectorPairLink (throws on malformed input with the same messages as buildPhonePairLink) and parseConnectorPairLink (null unless every part is well formed). Add export * from "./connector-pairing" to packages/contracts/src/index.ts after line 44. Write the test file.

items.title: buildConnectorPairLink returns 'overdeck-connector:/pair#v=1&e=<environmentId>&k=<machineKeyHex>&c=<code>' and parseConnectorPairLink of that string returns the same three fields
buildConnectorPairLink throws for an uppercase machine key, a non-UUID environment id and a code without the odp_ prefix
parseConnectorPairLink returns null for a phone link, for v=2 and for a missing c parameter, and parsePhonePairLink returns null for a connector string
Store connector pairing intents by pairingId

narrative.Action: Follow PRD W-4, D-6 and D-7. Create src/dashboard/server/connector-pairing.ts (under 120 lines) exporting ConnectorPairingIntent, issueConnectorPairing({ name, scopes }), takeConnectorIntent(pairingId), hasConnectorIntent(pairingId), isConnectorCode(code) and _resetConnectorPairingForTests(). issueConnectorPairing calls issuePairingCredential(), derives pairingId with pairingSecrets(nodeCrypto, credential).pairingId, prunes entries older than expiresAt + PAIRING_CREDENTIAL_TTL_MS, stores { name, scopes, expiresAt } in a module-level Map keyed by pairingId, and returns { pairingString: buildConnectorPairLink({ environmentId, machineKeyHex, code }), expiresAt } using ensureEnvironmentIdentity() and publicKeyHex(await ensureMachineKey()). takeConnectorIntent removes the entry on every call and returns it only when not expired. hasConnectorIntent is read-only and true for any stored entry, expired or not. Tests use fake timers for expiry (repo rule fake-timers-for-retry-tests).

items.title: Given a temp OVERDECK_HOME, issueConnectorPairing returns a pairingString that parseConnectorPairLink accepts, with e equal to the environment id and k equal to the machine key reported by buildEnvironmentDescriptor()

takeConnectorIntent returns the intent with the issued name and scopes on the first call, returns null on the second call, and hasConnectorIntent then returns false
